plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure, aligning with capital preservation.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single-name mandate.
Reduce CRWD to 10% and SMH to 5% to further diversify and manage sector concentration.
Buy ALB at 10% to add a new, high-scoring quality name and diversify the portfolio.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a target of ~1.5% per month. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration, but still carries market exposure.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure while maintaining a small allocation.
Reduce SPY to 25% to meet the single-name concentration mandate.
Buy ALB at 4% to introduce a new, high-scoring name for diversification.
Add to CRWD, increasing it to 16%, to lean into a strong performing quality tech name.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% per month by blending broad index exposure with quality tech and a small amount of leverage. It aims for growth with a focus on risk management, maintaining moderate market exposure.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single-name concentration mandate.
Add to SOXL and SPAL, increasing each to 6%, to lean into leveraged ETFs for higher growth potential.
Buy ALB at 6% to add a new, high-scoring name to the portfolio.
Increase CRWD to 16% and SMH to 15% to concentrate in strong performing tech and semiconductor sectors.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% per month by stretching growth through increased leverage and concentration. This approach significantly raises both upside potential and drawdown risk, with leveraged ETFs subject to daily decay and rebalancing. Strict stop discipline is crucial to manage potential rapid losses.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure, prioritizing low drawdown.
Add to QQQI, increasing it to 30%, to boost monthly distributions and income focus.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single-name mandate.
Reduce CRWD to 5% and SMH to 5% to minimize exposure to high-beta single names and sectors.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1% per month by rotating into income-generating ETFs and broad index funds. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income over growth, but distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in market selloffs.
